title: Autoguide field-repair kits and synthetic playflows for support automation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a packaged set of self-contained 'field-repair kits' (collections of scripted runbook tasks, guardrails, and parameterized playflows) that on-call engineers and Support Automation can execute autonomously to recover degraded inference capacity or persistent KV cache regressions. The kits should be accessible from the Console and the ops CLI, safe-by-default (dry-run, approval gates), instrumented for post-action telemetry, and designed to be composable into synthetic playflows for routine validation and training of incident responders.
motivation: We frequently see recurring incident patterns where engineers run a sequence of manual commands that are brittle and poorly instrumented. Packaging these sequences as curated, testable repair kits reduces mean time to repair (MTTR), documents tribal knowledge, and enables automated periodic validation so issues are detected earlier.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Field-repair kits implement 5 canonical scenarios (cache flush + warm, model fallback switch, node restart + graceful drain, autoscaler health-reset, quota reconciliation). 2) Each kit exposes dry-run, preview, and execute modes with RBAC checks. 3) Kits are registered in the Console with a one-click run UX and CLI counterpart. 4) Executions emit structured telemetry events to the ops-dashboard and create an attachable incident timeline entry. 5) Two synthetic playflows built from kits run in CI and in a scheduled Canary job and surface regressions to the SLO-runbook channel.
technical_notes: We will implement kits as runbooks-as-tasks backed by the existing playflow DSL (extend with 'guard' and 'probe' primitives). For safety, the execute command will require token-approval and will run in a sandboxed orchestration pod with a dry-run path that validates API calls. Leverage the Agentlet runflow queue for parallel-safe execution and reuse existing KV-caching APIs for warmups. Avoid adding any privileged cross-account actions; use role-scoped tokens and per-customer scoping in Private deployments.
implementation_steps: Define canonical scenarios and derive step templates (3 days)
Extend playflow DSL with guard/probe/conditional retries (4 days)
Build Console registry UI and CLI integration (3 days)
Telemetry schema for kit runs and incident timeline linkbacks (2 days)
Create initial 5 kits and two synthetic playflows, add CI jobs (3 days)
Run safety review and limited canary with Platform SRE (2 days)
rollback_plan: All execute-mode actions are reversible where possible; each kit must include an explicit 'undo' step or a compensating transaction. If an execution produces unexpected errors, the orchestration shuts down further steps and posts a rollback suggestion to the incident timeline. Console will offer a one-click revert that calls the kit's undo path.
metrics_to_monitor: Number of manual steps avoided per incident
rollout_plan: Phase 1: internal alpha for SRE and 2 oncall teams (1 week). Phase 2: wider rollout to Support, enable Console catalog, schedule synthetic playflows in Canary (2 weeks). Phase 3: enable on Private deployments behind opt-in and publish docs/playbook (2 weeks). Monitor metrics and run a postmortem after first production use.
test_plan: Unit tests for DSL primitives, integration tests for orchestration sandbox, end-to-end smoke tests that run in a non-prod infra with mocks, and CI jobs executing synthetic playflows nightly. Add manual runbook QA with SRE to validate safety-gates.
